Readable stories about the Oscars: who predicts well, which precursor awards help, and what the evidence can—and cannot—tell us.

::: {.callout-note title="Project status: foundation in progress"}
This is an early, static project homepage, not a completed analysis or forecast service. No model has been trained, no historical backtest results are published, and **no actual 2027 probabilities are available**.
:::

## First story, when the evidence is ready {#first-story}

**Which precursor awards actually help?**

The planned article will compare category-specific precursor agreement and test whether those signals improve predictions in later, unseen seasons. Publication depends on verified source permissions, dated inputs, reviewed coverage, and a frozen evaluation—not on finding a surprising result. A negative or inconclusive finding is worth reporting.

A comparison of pundits and consensus forecasts may lead instead if its data and reuse permissions are verified first. A later story will explore box office while separating descriptive lifetime revenue from information available before a forecast.

*There is no published article yet.* Articles and selected technical notebooks will be added individually after review; this milestone publishes only Home.

## How this will work {#methods}

Articles will lead with a clear question, auditable denominators, uncertainty, and limitations. Methods and selected notebooks will explain how each finding can be reproduced.

Only approved public extracts and reviewed saved results will support published analysis. Acquisition and training stay separate from the website build. This homepage requires no datasets, live APIs, or running Python server.

### Known limitations

- The 2010–2026 window is a target, not a claim of complete data.
- Category definitions and field sizes change across ceremonies; comparisons must account for those changes.
- Predictive agreement is not evidence that a precursor award or revenue causes an Oscar win.
- There are no interactive charts, article findings, or forecasts to inspect yet.
